newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Patten hopes China troops will set example.
newsitem.headline: HK's Patten hopes China troops will set example.

text.p: Governor Chris Patten said on Monday he hoped the first troops from China's army to enter Hong Kong would set a good example and help ensure a smooth transfer of sovereignty.

"I hope it will ensure that the garrison arrives smoothly and efficiently in the future and performs the role assigned to it," Patten told reporters after a 40-strong People's Liberation Army (PLA) advance party drove into the British colony to prepare garrison facilities.

The PLA will take over defence duties from the British when London hands back Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30 after more than a century and a half of colonial rule. The PLA's role is spelled out in a new garrison law and in a handover treaty.
The advance party, led by Major-General Zhou Borong, will lay the ground for a garrison of up to 10,000 PLA soldiers after July 1.

Although the PLA's arrival has unnerved some Hong Kong people who remember the bloody crushing of China's pro-democracy movement in 1989, Patten said he was confident the advance party would behave well to gain Hong Kong people's trust.

"I am sure that the garrison commanders and the garrison members will want to give the best possible example of how the PLA behaves and I am sure that will go for this advance deployment as well," he said.
The arrival of the unarmed unit with 71 days to go before Britain hands over its last important colony was low-key and left many of the wealthy territory's more than six million people unmoved.
Patten said he expected the advance party would get along well with the British troops still in Hong Kong.
"I am sure that they will work sensibly together. They are professional, they are soldiers. Soldiers invariably get on well with other soldiers," he said.
